textbookText: Figure 8.1.1 Five kingdom classification Protistans consist of microscopic, single-celled and primitive eukaryotic organisms. This group includes diverse living organisms that are plant-like, such as golden algae and diatoms, animals like such as Paramecium and Amoeba. Some of them are both plants and animals like such as Euglena and Astasia and some of them are fungi like such as Fuligo, Protostelium, etc.

Organisms belonging to the protista have following features: 1. They are usually aquatic and some of them are also found in moist soil. 2. They are simple, microscopic and unicellular eukaryotes. Some protist like Volvox is colonial. 3. They have protoplasmic or acellular level of body organization. 4. Cell body is externally covered by cell membrane or cell wall and some of them are without any outer covering. 5. They have either single nucleus (monomorphic) or two nuclei (dimorphic condition) in Paramecium or many nuclei (coenocytic condition) in Opalina. 6. Their locomotion takes place with the help of pseudopodia, flagella and cilia. In some forms, there may not be locomotory organs. 7. Mode of nutrition is different among them. They show holophytic or holozoic or mixotrophic or saprozoic or parasitic mode of nutrition. 8. Digestion of food particles takes place inside the cell (intracellular digestion). 9. Respiration and excretion take place through general body surface. 10. Reproduction takes place asexually by binary fission, multiple fission, cyst formation, sporulation etc. Sexual reproduction takes place by conjugation and fusion of gametes (syngamy).

Some protistans are planktons. Planktons are those creatures which are free swimming on the surface of water. They are autotrophic plant like, called phytoplankton (Diatoms) and heterotrophic animal like, called zooplankton (paramecium).
